subject: Nvidia rehired Huang. Markets added $950 billion.
bodyMarkdown:
If you hold a Canadian index fund or a group RRSP, you made money yesterday because one man got his job back. I want to explain why that should bother you a little, even if you enjoyed the gain.

## What the board actually said

Nvidia told the SEC on November 12 that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately, with chief financial officer Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO. Eleven days later the same board voted unanimously to bring him back. The company's November 23 filing says the directors found his candour satisfactory, that they took input from senior levels of the United States government, and that his return poses no national security risk. CNBC reported on Monday that what sealed the decision was a personal assurance from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws. Trump told CNBC, "I made the deal." Fox News reported that the resignation followed an investigation into a reported affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence source. Nvidia has not confirmed that part.

## One man, $950 billion

Nvidia closed Monday up 31.5% at $165.05, which several outlets counted as roughly $950 billion of market value added in one session. The Washington Post put the figure closer to $1 trillion. Yahoo Finance reported the stock traded up as much as 35% intraday and that the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all posted their best day since April 2025, with the Nasdaq up about 6.5%. Here is the part that reaches a Canadian saver. Nvidia's **index weight**, meaning the share of a fund's money sitting in that one stock, was 5.70% of State Street's SPDR S&P 500 ETF as of November 19, and 24/7 Wall St. calculated that Nvidia alone produced about a third of that fund's gain on Monday. Closer to home, the S&P/TSX composite rose 939.15 points to 34,129.00 according to Canadian Press, and Reuters reported Canadian tech up 5.5% with Celestica up 11%.

## What is still open

No legal question closed on Monday. Trefis noted on November 23 that Nvidia faces a reported SEC disclosure inquiry dated November 17 and an investigative subpoena from California attorney general Rob Bonta dated November 19, and that neither the company nor Huang has been charged with anything. The board also created a National Security and Export Control Committee staffed only by independent directors, which tells you where the directors think the real exposure sits. The stock is also still far below where it was in the autumn. 24/7 Wall St. reported it finished last week 47.5% under its October 6 record, so a 31.5% day recovers part of a much bigger fall, not the whole thing. Meanwhile the macro calendar is indifferent to all of it.

## The takeaway

I am watching December 9, when the Fed and the Bank of Canada both decide. Futures and prediction markets had a quarter-point Fed hike close to certain as of Monday, which would lift the target range to 4.00% to 4.25%, while CBC reported that economists expect the Bank of Canada to hold at 2.50% after October inflation printed 3.1%. If you own a broad index fund, open the holdings page and look at what percentage sits in the top ten names, because Monday showed you how much of your return rides on one boardroom. I would not trade on any of this, but I would know the number.
